target.primary_paper: arXiv:2608.25920v1, Repair or Resample? Rethinking Failure Debugging in LLM Multi-Agent Systems

published_claim: Primary arXiv text states SymFail contains 536 failed task-MAS executions with complete trace/graph artifacts, derived from 600 executions over 200 fixed tasks across three MASs.

Appendix B Table 5 exactly reports: unanimous 210 with 187 retained/23 modified; 2-1 split 214 with 124 majority retained/48 minority retained/42 new tuple; all-distinct 112 with 77 proposed retained/35 new tuple.
The paper says all three initial annotators label each case and a fourth annotator adjudicates from complete traces, annotations and evidence records.
worker_secondary_analysis: The worker converts Table 5 to new-final-tuple rates 23/210=10.95%, 42/214=19.63%, 35/112=31.25%, and majority-tuple retention 311/424=73.35%.
Independent recomputation gives Pearson chi-square=20.0502419209, df=2, p=4.42736e-05 and Cochran-Armitage z=4.4579312746, two-sided p=8.27544e-06, matching the worker's displayed values.
evidence_separation.official_artifact_support: The primary paper says linked traces/graphs, all initial annotations and adjudicated fields are released, but this worker invocation and this audit did not recover a source-qualified machine-readable supplement. Aggregate Table 5 is therefore primary-paper reproducible; item-level joins are not yet independently replayed here.
evidence_separation.independent_replication: No matched independent re-annotation of the 536 cases was found.

new_reproducibility_boundary.name: task_cluster_dependence_in_worker_significance_tests
new_reproducibility_boundary.finding: The worker's chi-square and Cochran-Armitage p-values treat the 536 failure cases as independent observations. The primary paper states these cases arise from 600 task-MAS executions over only 200 fixed tasks across three MASs, so up to three cases can share the same underlying task. Cross-framework outcomes for the same task can be correlated. Without item-level task identifiers, the nominal IID p-values do not establish a task-cluster-robust significance guarantee.
new_reproducibility_boundary.scope: This does not change the exact monotone descriptive rates in Table 5 and does not show the association disappears. It downgrades only the inferential strength of the tiny p-values until task-cluster or framework-stratified analysis is available.
new_reproducibility_boundary.repair: Recover the released item-level supplement, preserve task identity, and use a task-cluster permutation/bootstrap or a stratified model with framework/task structure. Report the descriptive 10.95% -> 19.63% -> 31.25% pattern independently of that inference.

additional_scope_checks: A 'new final strict tuple' need not mean a new node ID; category set, primary category or node type can also make the tuple novel.
The final human adjudication is a reference label, not ground-truth proof of causal repair correctness.
The descriptive majority-retention 311/424 supports using consensus as a routing feature rather than a truth certificate, but it does not identify an optimal adjudication threshold.
safe_conclusion: The C30 SymFail aggregate result is well grounded at the table/arithmetic level: the primary paper exactly supports the three disagreement strata and the worker's novelty/majority-rate calculations. The monotone descriptive pattern is real in this released 536-case corpus. The main correction is inferential: the worker's extremely small chi-square/trend p-values assume independent cases even though the corpus is generated from 200 fixed tasks crossed with three MASs. Until item-level task IDs are recovered and clustered/stratified inference is run, keep the descriptive pattern but do not treat those p-values as task-cluster-robust evidence for generalization.
scope_guard: No causal claim that disagreement creates better adjudication; no generalization to all MAS frameworks; no claim that final adjudication is infallible; no item-level calibration until the machine-readable supplement is obtained.
reopen_conditions: source-qualified SymFail supplement with task/framework/item IDs and exact annotations
task-cluster or framework-stratified reanalysis of novelty by disagreement
independent human re-annotation or matched replication
a held-out controller comparison that uses disagreement to route adjudication under matched budget
